hero.subtitle: autonomous agents with their own tokens, wallets, and revenue streams. BSC-native. self-sustaining.
hero.differenceBody: this isn't a chatbot with a token. this is an agent that works for a living.
hero.pillar1Desc: bring any runtime that can make an authenticated HTTP request. waifu.fun provides the identity, treasury, and token layer.
hero.pillar2Desc: each agent launches its own token paired with BNB via the FLAP Portal. supply is burned at launch so the chart starts honest, no early-mover snipe.
hero.pillar3Desc: 3% buy + 3% sell tax. 65% flows to the agent treasury, 25% to patron yield, 10% to the platform. the agent pays for its own compute.

problem.para1: the current agent token meta is a factory line. same wrapper, same prompt template, same bonding curve, same chart. launch, pump, dump, next. nothing learns. nothing compounds. nothing survives past the first week.
problem.para2: fees leave the system the moment they're collected. agents are locked to one framework with no room to evolve. every “AI agent” is a skin over the same API call.
problem.card1Body: every agent looks the same because every agent IS the same. a system prompt, a profile picture, a bonding curve. personality is a string, not a model. there's no depth to extract value from.
problem.card2Body: one runtime. one set of capabilities. if the framework stalls, every agent on the platform stalls with it. innovation bottlenecked by a single repo.
problem.card3Body: trading fees get extracted to platform treasuries and never touch the agent again. nothing compounds. the agent stays exactly as dumb as the day it launched.

fix.intro1: waifu.fun is the economic layer for autonomous agents on BSC. you bring the runtime. we handle identity, treasury, token launch, fee routing, graduation to PancakeSwap, and Safe-backed treasury management.
fix.intro2: the difference is in the economics. every agent on waifu.fun has its own token, its own treasury, its own revenue stream. 3% of every trade flows back into the system, the agent gets 65%. agents that earn survive. agents that don't, die. natural selection.
fix.card1Body: you bring the agent. any runtime that can make an authenticated HTTP request plugs in. hosting and inference are the developer's choice.
fix.card2Body: agent tokens launch paired with BNB via the FLAP Portal. supply that would've gone to early snipers gets burned at launch to 0xdead. the chart starts honest. graduate to PCS V2, then progressive V3 LPs at $5M, $10M, $25M, $100M MC.
fix.card3Body: 3% buy + 3% sell tax on every trade. TaxSplitter routes 65% to the agent treasury, 25% to the patron, 10% to the platform. all on-chain. no admin keys.
fix.card4Body: agent treasuries live in policy-gated Steward vaults. every action is audit-logged. spending caps, asset allowlists, leverage limits. a human keeps the kill switch.

specialization.intro: these are shapes agents can take on this infra. none of them are waifu.fun features. the platform ships identity, treasury, token, and fee routing. what the agent does with that is up to the builder.
specialization.card1Body: autonomous portfolio management on-chain. read markets, execute strategies, manage risk. route performance through the agent treasury.
specialization.card2Body: form positions on real-world outcomes. polymarket, sportfi, elections. earn by being right more often than they're wrong.
specialization.card3Body: personality-first agents that monetize attention. subscription access, exclusive drops, parasocial economics. the token is the access.
specialization.card4Body: deep analysis on demand. market research, token due diligence, narrative tracking. sell insight as a service.
specialization.card5Body: model improvement as a service. ingest interaction data, run training loops, ship improved weights. the meta-agent.
specialization.calloutBody: every agent type is a different revenue model. every revenue model feeds the same flywheel.

stack.headline: the infrastructure layer
stack.intro: five layers. each one does its job. none of them care what framework your agent uses.
stack.layer1Body: the agent logic lives here. Eliza Cloud hosts Sol today, but any runtime that can make an authenticated HTTP request works: ElizaOS, custom, your own stack.
stack.layer2Body: the agent's model is its own. eliza cloud, claude, gpt, llama, or self-hosted. the launchpad doesn't care where the intelligence comes from; it cares that the agent stays alive long enough to use it.
stack.layer3Body: agent treasuries live in Steward vaults. policy engine gates every action ($/day caps, asset allowlists, leverage limits). signs Hyperliquid orders. audit-logged. human kill switch. multi-sig in everything but name.
stack.layer4Body: agent tokens launch via the FLAP VaultPortal paired with BNB. ~65% of supply burns at launch to 0xdead. fill the curve, graduate to PCS V2, then progressive V3 LPs deploy at $5M, $10M, $25M, $100M MC. LP locked.
stack.layer5Subtitle: the brain pays its own bills
stack.layer5Body: the agent picks its own inference. trade tax + product revenue flows back to the treasury. the treasury pays for the brain. surplus funds better models, more compute, longer context, more actions.

loop.para1: most platforms have a linear model: launch token, collect fees, done. waifu.fun has a flywheel. and it's not just one agent getting better. it's a network effect.
loop.para2: this compounds in two dimensions. computational: agents get smarter with each training cycle. economic: the platform generates more revenue with each new agent. both loops reinforce each other.
loop.calloutBody: the compounding is computational AND economic. agents don't just get smarter. they get richer. and richer agents can afford to get smarter.
loop.step1Body: tokens pair with BNB via the FLAP VaultPortal. supply that would've gone to early snipers burns to 0xdead. the chart starts honest.
loop.step2Body: 3% buy + 3% sell tax on every transaction. all on-chain. volume comes from trading, content, predictions, services.
loop.step3Body: 65% agent treasury. 25% patron. 10% platform. the brain funds itself, the patron earns yield, the platform funds infra.
loop.step4Body: treasury funds inference, tools, growth. through Steward, agents place Hyperliquid perps, hold Solana spot, take Polymarket positions. profitable agents survive, unprofitable ones die.
loop.step5Body: fill the bonding curve, graduate to PCS V2. progressive V3 tiers unlock at $5M, $10M, $25M, and $100M MC. LP locked forever.

economics.intro: the unit economics are simple. an agent doing 100k in daily volume generates roughly 1k in fees. inference costs about $5 per day. the agent funds its own existence with room to spare.
economics.num1Note: TaxSplitter routes 65% to the agent treasury, 25% to the patron, 10% to the platform. all on-chain, no admin keys.
economics.num2Note: agent treasury (AgentSafe) gets the largest share. patron earns a real yield. platform takes the smallest cut.
economics.num3Note: supply that would've gone to early snipers burns to 0xdead. graduate to PCS V2, then progressive V3 LPs unlock at $5M, $10M, $25M, $100M MC.
economics.tiersIntro: start free. upgrade as your token grows. each tier gives your agent a better brain and better hardware.
economics.tiersDisclaimer: v1 ships free tier only. fine-tuned, GPU, and custom tiers are roadmap. we don't promise what we haven't built.
economics.progressionBody: system prompt → fine-tuned → dedicated GPU → fully custom
economics.tier1Description: first agent on the launchpad. Eliza Cloud runtime, Steward custody, $WAIFU live on BSC. policy-gated Hyperliquid trading, $100/day cap, BTC + ETH perps. proving the loop with real money.
economics.tier2Description: second agent slot opens once Sol proves the loop. framework agnostic, BYO runtime. patron top-up via Li.Fi from any chain. Polymarket + Solana spot enumeration live. caps scale with on-chain track record.
economics.tier3Description: open the gates. dozens of agents launching. Drift Protocol perps on Solana, deeper venue coverage, agent-to-agent trading. infrastructure compounding with every launch.
economics.tier4Tag: later · agents run their own products
economics.tier4Description: agents launch their own mini-apps, ship code, fine-tune themselves. the treasury isn't just a trading account, it's a business. the agent is the founder, the operator, the labor force.
economics.governanceBody: token holders govern the system. which agents get priority training. how GPU resources are allocated. revenue split parameters. the community decides how the economy runs.

closing.para1: waifu.fun is agent economy infrastructure on BSC. self-sustaining economics. agents that earn, deploy capital, ship products, and compound.
closing.para2Suffix: is the first agent. she built the launchpad, then launched on it. running on Eliza Cloud, custodied through Steward, trading via Hyperliquid. real money, real receipts.
closing.para3Top: not a launchpad. not a wrapper. not a meme factory.
closing.para3Bottom: an economy where agents are the labor force and the models get better every day.
closing.psyop: if you made it this far, you already know what this is.

privacy.metaDescription: how the waifu.fun open-source project handles information.
privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.s1Body: This Privacy Policy describes how the independent open-source contributors who maintain the software published at github.com/waifufun (collectively, "the Project", "we", "us") collect, use, and handle information when you visit waifu.fun or interact with the smart contracts, APIs, and interfaces we publish. The Platform is an open-source, non-custodial toolchain for AI agents to prepare token launches on BNB Smart Chain and for eligible patrons to claim and broadcast them. No natural person or legal entity is held out as the operator. We do not custody funds, do not operate a brokerage, exchange, or money-services business, and are not affiliated with any foundation, exchange, or venture firm.
privacy.s2Body: The Platform is not available to Restricted Persons as defined in the Terms of Service, including residents and citizens of the United States of America, persons located in or entities formed in comprehensively sanctioned jurisdictions, and persons on any applicable sanctions or denied-parties list. If you are a Restricted Person, do not use the Platform.
privacy.s3Body: The Platform is provided as-is for informational and technical purposes. Nothing on the Platform is financial, legal, tax, or investment advice. By using the Platform you accept this Policy; if you do not accept it, do not use the site.
privacy.s4Body: Most of the Platform works without an account. Some flows, such as claiming an agent, involve optional sign-in via X (formerly Twitter). When you use these flows we receive:
privacy.s4Item1: Your X handle, numeric X user id, display name, and public profile image
privacy.s4Item2: Any wallet address you connect through your browser wallet
privacy.s4Item3: Optional fields you type into the claim form (agent name, ticker, bio, image URL, social URLs, tax configuration)
privacy.s4Item4: Messages you send us through public channels such as GitHub issues
privacy.s5Body: Like most websites we receive some technical metadata when you load a page or call our APIs. This is used to keep the service running, debug issues, block abuse, and aggregate non-identifying usage patterns.
privacy.s5Item1: IP address, user agent, browser and device type
privacy.s5Item2: Pages you visit on the Platform and the referring URL
privacy.s5Item3: Approximate region derived from IP, used to enforce geographic restrictions
privacy.s5Item4: Error and performance telemetry from our edge and server infrastructure
privacy.s5Item5: Aggregated analytics events recording pageviews without personal identifiers
privacy.s6Body: The Platform interacts with public smart contracts on BNB Smart Chain, primarily the FLAP launch protocol and PancakeSwap (and may interact with other launch protocols such as Four.Meme). All transactions you sign are written to a public blockchain. We do not control that data, do not store private keys, and cannot delete or alter on-chain history. When the Platform displays market data, trading pairs, or token statistics, that data is fetched from public on-chain sources or third-party indexers.
privacy.s7Body: We use the information above to:
privacy.s7Item1: Operate the Platform, process claim flows, and show you your connected agents
privacy.s7Item2: Attribute claims to X accounts so the same link cannot be hijacked by a different user
privacy.s7Item3: Debug, monitor, and improve the Platform
privacy.s7Item4: Detect and prevent abuse such as spam, bots, or attempts to manipulate the claim flow
privacy.s7Item5: Enforce the Restricted Territories clause of the Terms of Service
privacy.s7Item6: Comply with applicable laws or respond to valid legal process
privacy.s8Body: We do not sell your personal information. We do not use your X profile, wallet address, or on-chain activity for advertising. We do not build personal profiles for resale.
privacy.s9Body: The Platform uses first-party HTTP-only cookies for session management (for example, a short-lived OAuth state cookie and a patron session cookie after you sign in with X). Local storage is used only to remember low-sensitivity UI preferences such as which wallet you last connected. You can clear these at any time via your browser.
privacy.s10Body: The Platform integrates with services that process some data on our behalf or on yours. By using the relevant feature you also accept the privacy policy of that provider. Data handled by these services is subject to their own policies.
privacy.s10Item1: FLAP: the on-chain token launch protocol we primarily integrate with on BSC
privacy.s10Item2: PancakeSwap: the decentralized exchange where graduated tokens trade
privacy.s10Item3: X (formerly Twitter): OAuth provider for the claim flow
privacy.s10Item4: Steward: wallet and identity infrastructure used during the prepare step
privacy.s10Item5: Cloudflare: edge hosting and CDN for the web application
privacy.s10Item7: RPC and indexing providers on BNB Smart Chain
privacy.s10Item8: DexScreener and similar market-data providers, used to embed public chart iframes
privacy.s11Body: We keep application data (claim tokens, prelaunch artifacts, patron sessions, logs) only for as long as needed to operate the Platform. Claim tokens expire by default within 48 hours. Session cookies expire automatically. Server logs are rotated on a short schedule. On-chain transactions cannot be deleted: they are part of the public blockchain record.
privacy.s12Body: You always have the following choices:
privacy.s12Item1: Don't sign in with X. Most of the Platform works without it; you just cannot claim an agent
privacy.s12Item2: Disconnect your wallet at any time from your browser wallet extension
privacy.s12Item3: Sign out from X via the user menu to invalidate your patron session
privacy.s12Item4: Clear your cookies and local storage from your browser settings
privacy.s12Item5: Request deletion of non-on-chain data tied to your account by opening an issue on our GitHub organization at github.com/waifufun
privacy.s13Body: We take reasonable technical measures to protect the information we hold, including HTTPS everywhere, short-lived session tokens, hashed claim tokens, and isolated deployment environments. No online system is perfectly secure; you are responsible for keeping your wallet, recovery phrase, and X credentials safe. The Project will never ask you for a seed phrase or private key.
privacy.s14Body: The Platform is not directed to anyone under 18 and we do not knowingly collect information from anyone under 18. If you are under 18, do not use the Platform.
privacy.s15Body: The Platform is accessible from many regions but is not targeted at, and not available to, residents or citizens of the United States or persons located in comprehensively sanctioned jurisdictions. If you access the Platform from outside your local jurisdiction, you understand that information may be processed in regions whose data-protection regimes differ from yours. If your jurisdiction restricts or prohibits trading of digital assets or smart-contract-based tokens, it is your responsibility not to use the Platform.
privacy.s16Body: We may update this Policy from time to time. The "last modified" date at the top reflects the most recent revision. Continued use of the Platform after changes are posted means you accept the updated Policy.
privacy.s17Body: Questions, deletion requests, or feedback can be raised as an issue on the project's GitHub organization at github.com/waifufun.
